- Clarify VAT treatment — UK side will provide VAT ID; do you apply reverse-charge or charge VAT?
- Any impact to outstanding PO / payment terms — we have a signed PO on file (attached).

Can you loop in finance and confirm what you’ll need from us to generate the two invoices and keep payment timing intact?

Hi all —

We can implement the split. Attached is a draft proration workbook (20261004-kestrel-proration-estimate.xlsx) — summary below. We used day-level proration (charges allocated by number of billable days in period) which matches how your PO was constructed. If you prefer second-level billing we can rerun but day-level is standard.

Summary (example numbers, USD):
- Full monthly capacity charge (Oct): $120,000
- Days billed in period: 31
- Oct 1–9 (9 days) -> charged fully to US parent for those days = (120,000 / 31 * 9) = $34,838.71
- Oct 10–31 (22 days) -> total for period = (120,000 / 31 * 22) = $85,161.29
  - Allocate 60% to Kestrel Therapeutics Inc (US): $51,096.77
  - Allocate 40% to Kestrel Therapeutics UK Ltd (UK): $34,064.52

Suggested invoice workflow:
1) Issue an invoice to Kestrel Therapeutics Inc for the US-only portion (Oct 1–9 + 60% of Oct 10–31) = $85,935.48 (net) — no VAT expected for US entity.
2) Issue an invoice to Kestrel Therapeutics UK Ltd for the UK-allocated portion (40% of Oct 10–31) = $34,064.52.

VAT / tax note:
- For the UK invoice, if Kestrel UK provides a valid EU/UK VAT ID and the supply qualifies, we can apply the reverse-charge (customer self-account for VAT). We will need the VAT ID and billing address for Kestrel UK to validate against the VIES/UK VAT register. If validation fails, we may need to charge UK VAT at the local rate.

Please confirm the legal entity names, billing addresses, VAT ID for Kestrel UK, and whether you want us to keep the original payment due date (we can schedule both invoices with the same due date).

Attachments: 20261004-kestlation-proration-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)

— Marissa
